entry.title: the 1972 collapse (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the 1972 collapse of the Sidney Lanier Bridge (pictured), which was caused by a collision with a cargo ship, caused ten deaths and over a million dollars in damages?

entry.title: Christian death metal (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Christian death metal has been called the least likely musical development at the close of the 20th century?

entry.title: An Introduction to Non-Classical Logic (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the second edition of An Introduction to Non-Classical Logic more than doubled the length of the original text?

entry.title: Jama Masjid (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Wolseley Haig noted that it was not the "city's huge mosque" but the "far less pretentious" Jama Masjid that served as the congregational mosque in Hyderabad?

entry.title: Esus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the violent end of a bog body might be related to the cult of the Celtic god Esus?

entry.title: tornadoes in Oklahoma's history (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the three costliest tornadoes in Oklahoma's history hit the same town in 2013, in 1999 and in 2003?

entry.title: a TV station in Windsor, Ontario (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a TV station in Windsor, Ontario, was spared from closure even though it lost money for ten consecutive years?

entry.title: spiked savoury (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the leaves of the herb spiked savoury, although protected under Israeli law, are foraged by local people to make a spice mix?

entry.title: black holes in fiction (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the earliest black holes in fiction appeared decades before the term black hole was coined?
